params.name: nacute
params.let: len([x for x in v if x < 90])

params.name: nright
params.let: len([x for x in v if x == 90])

params.name: nobtuse
params.let: len([x for x in v if x > 90 and x < 180])

params.name: nstraight
params.let: len([x for x in v if x == 180])

params.name: nreflex
params.let: len([x for x in v if x > 180])

params.why: the count is never 0 or 5 or 6, so it cannot be guessed from the shape of the list

params.require: len([x for x in v if abs(x - 90) <= 1 or abs(x - 180) <= 1]) >= 2
params.why: at least two boundary angles (89, 90, 91 or 179, 180, 181) so the book's near-right twist appears in every instance

stem: Six angles measure ${=v[0]}^\circ$, ${=v[1]}^\circ$, ${=v[2]}^\circ$, ${=v[3]}^\circ$, ${=v[4]}^\circ$ and ${=v[5]}^\circ$. How many of these six angles are obtuse angles?
solution: An obtuse angle is bigger than $90^\circ$ and smaller than $180^\circ$. An angle of exactly $90^\circ$ is a right angle and one of exactly $180^\circ$ is a straight angle, so neither of those is obtuse.
Put the angles in order of size: ${=w[0]}^\circ$, ${=w[1]}^\circ$, ${=w[2]}^\circ$, ${=w[3]}^\circ$, ${=w[4]}^\circ$, ${=w[5]}^\circ$.

Compare each angle with the limits $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$. Acute (smaller than $90^\circ$): {=nacute}; right (exactly $90^\circ$): {=nright}; obtuse (between $90^\circ$ and $180^\circ$): {=nobtuse}; straight (exactly $180^\circ$): {=nstraight}; reflex (bigger than $180^\circ$): {=nreflex}.
So {=nobtuse} of the six angles are obtuse.
notes: Advanced because it asks for six classifications at once and always includes at least two boundary angles (89/90/91 or 179/180/181): the book itself uses a 91 degree angle as its twist (ex 7.8 no. 1f). Pool of 16 angles with every type present (acute 4, right 1, obtuse 5, straight 1, reflex 5); the mid-range values shift together by j (0 to 9) and never cross a type boundary (largest acute 79 or 89, smallest obtuse 91, largest obtuse 162 or 179, largest reflex 327). The sample is six distinct angles; the obtuse count is 1 to 4 (a Python simulation of the sampling gave about 74 percent of draws accepted and about 14,900 distinct angle sets in 20,000 draws). No angle of 0 or 360 occurs. The worked solution is numeric only (sorted list and a count per type), so every step is true for each instance.
